appDelegations.nativeOverview: Maintain one business root Agent. Your trusted backend authenticates each user and resolves their own long-term isolated branch.
appDelegations.publishedOverview: This authorization uses a published assistant definition and its private instance. Follow the assistant Session API guide.
appDelegations.currentAccessHint: This status describes the authorization record. Requests also require current account, application and workspace access.
appDelegations.nativeGuideHint: Resolve a stable authenticated business user first, then use the returned branch Agent and branch header for all input and read requests.
appDelegations.publishedGuideHint: Obtain your private assistant instance, select an enabled models[].id from GET /api/models as modelConfigRef, then create a Session, submit messages and consume its events. This instance is shared by your account and definition; it does not isolate external business users.
appDelegations.deliveryHint: Accepted means the input is stored. Actual Read means the Agent has observed it. Neither means the task is complete. Only committed messages are user-facing output; one input can produce several messages or none.
appDelegations.cursorHint: A non-null nextAfterSequence continues the current page scan. The final page returns null. Deduplicate messages by id and save processed sourceSequence and valid scan progress; keep that progress at the final page.
appDelegations.readHint: Read updates the original accepted input. Keep pending inputs and their sequence, and query a window that includes them again; advancing an input cursor past them will not reveal later Read changes.
appDelegations.difyIdentity: Authenticate users on your backend and pass a stable Dify user. Use the trusted sys.user_id, not sys.conversation_id or an identity chosen by the model.
appDelegations.difyResolve: Keep the token in a Secret environment variable. Select that variable in the HTTP node's Bearer authorization without adding a second Bearer prefix. Construct request_body as an object in a Code node; select JSON body and reference the complete object variable shown below. Resolve businessUserId without the business-branch header.
appDelegations.difyConsume: Parse the HTTP response body with json.loads and extract agentId and branchId. Construct the input object with a retained inputId, then submit it with X-Centaeris-Business-Branch-Id. A backend consumer reads committed messages; keep the credential out of user browsers.
appDelegations.difyBoundary: This API is an asynchronous Agent stream. Its acceptance receipt is not a Dify answer. A synchronous bridge needs explicit message correlation, waiting, concurrency and recovery; the next message is not automatically the reply to one input.
appDelegations.nativeRetryHint: Retry with the same branch, exact body, inputId and authorization record. Rotation preserves the record. Changing the body returns 409 agent_input_conflict; another authorization cannot replay an old input (403 agent_input_source_forbidden).
appDelegations.publishedRetryHint: Use the published assistant message contract and retain the same request identity and content for uncertain retries. Select modelConfigRef from an enabled model id, not its display name.
appDelegations.errorHint: 401: check the current credential. 403: check scopes and current authority. 404: check the selected binding. 409: inspect the specific conflict. 410: do not replace a deleted branch with a new user identity. 503 admission busy: retry the same input after contention clears.
appDelegations.acceptedWorkHint: Rotation replaces the credential immediately. Revocation blocks new application requests. Both preserve existing branch identities and already accepted work.
appDelegations.workSessionsFailed: Unable to load this branch’s sessions. Check your access and try again.
appDelegations.workSessionsEmpty: No child work sessions are linked to this branch.
appDelegations.workSessionsMoreFailed: Unable to load more work sessions. Existing sessions are kept.

appDelegations.publishedWithdrawalHint: Rotation keeps this authorization and its records. Withdrawal blocks new application requests, and published-assistant Runs continue to check their delegated authority before protected operations.
appDelegations.sseHint: Reconnect using the actual opaque SSE frame id as Last-Event-ID, saved separately for each Run. Numeric sourceSequence is not this cursor. Live frames are transient; committed frames provide retained facts.
